sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"Mother, before ambition, give me the exact sustainable military picture: what is carried with the formations, what remains in depots and armories, what we can replace in food, arrows, bolts, armor and horses, and what a long campaign would consume. Father, I want House readiness judged before expansion. My Qin command is not permission to commit House Tang troops, treasury, reserves or workshops. Any deeper House participation must remain a separate family decision. I also want your view of what command prospects are realistically open to me and why you raised this now. For House posture, I want us to distinguish three states: garrison readiness, emergency mobilization, and sustained expeditionary campaigning, with different supply burdens for each. Father, give me the military judgment. Mother, give me the political and financial judgment. And I want both of you to understand how I personally fight. My doctrine is precision function denial: the shortest reliable line, no wasted movement, and attacks on exposed high-value anatomy to remove an enemy's ability to attack, see, stand, breathe or continue. Mounted with the bow, I use distance, mobility and deliberate high-value shots. With the lance, I preserve charge geometry and break away or reposition after contact rather than stop inside reach. Dismounted, I use shield and sword to control the weapon line, take the shortest opening, and grapple once the enemy's weapon is trapped, displaced or lost. Against named opponents, I decide whether the purpose is disable, capture or kill before that doctrine selects the efficient target.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_story_family_invitation_c92fc7096c3f37dc6a3b","request_id":"req_wei_family_council_full_position_r12_a","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"37f470725c45fe9e0c70594804b1f1105b0323a170c0355b1906a0c37411cac8","target_ref":"event_story_family_invitation_c92fc7096c3f37dc6a3b","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}

sword-interaction-attempt.v1 {"action":"present","actor_id":"char_tang_wei","formation_refs":[],"player_statement":"My field army doctrine is command by intent. I decide the army objective, major changes of plan, general withdrawal, major pursuit, irreversible escalation, and any commitment of protected House forces outside their established role. Lin Zhen keeps army-level coordination and command continuity under that intent, and succeeds me if I cannot command. Subordinate commanders receive problems appropriate to their level and decide how to solve them without waiting for me to micromanage every formation. In battle the sequence is observe, shape, fix, concentrate, break, exploit. I avoid even symmetrical fighting when local superiority can be created. Fix enemy strength, strike weakness, threaten one place to open another, probe to reveal reserves, use terrain, concealment, missile pressure, demonstrations, controlled withdrawals and maneuver as one system, preserve a meaningful reserve, rotate tired troops before cohesion fails, and avoid frontal attrition when maneuver is cheaper. Formation is physical geometry, so frontage, depth, spacing, facing, reach, shields, terrain and cohesion govern what methods work. Weapons change with geometry: missiles while lanes and range are useful, spear and shield while reach and spacing hold, sword and shield when contact compresses. Qin units fight the main battle. My House Guard protects my command position first and supports second. The Champions are the inner guard and precision counter-threat. Use terrain before blood, keep reserves fresh, concentrate where it matters, and use the simplest tactic that creates the required advantage.","posture":null,"process_ref":"event_story_family_invitation_c92fc7096c3f37dc6a3b","request_id":"repair_replay_wei_field_doctrine_r14_a","schema":"sword-interaction-attempt.v1","surface_digest":"e5c9065085e8615974279902ea5b265e3520a75a0d69d7fbdd98e935bd8e2731","target_ref":"char_tang_zhu","world_response_status":"not_established_by_attempt"}
